title: First-harmonic spectral lane: window phases, pivot anti-reconstruction and adjacent-window transport

concepts.label: window discrepancy A(h,N,L)
concepts.description: The depth-L integer truncation of 2^L·(R_{N+h} − R_N), whose residue mod 2^L carries the whole finite certificate.

concepts.label: endpoint kill certificate
concepts.description: The decidable predicate that A(h,N,L) mod 2^L avoids the radius-(N+h+L+2) neighbourhood of 0, so the tail difference is provably not an integer.

concepts.label: first additive character of the window residue
concepts.description: windowFirstCos / windowFirstExp: the real and complex first harmonic of the window residue on the dyadic circle.

concepts.label: room inequality 16(2X+h+L+2) ≤ 2^L
concepts.description: The depth budget under which the excluded certificate arcs are at most a sixteenth of the circle.

concepts.label: large-prime pivot and residual
concepts.description: Exact division of the window phase by a proposed one-dimensional prime phase, leaving a residual with no independence assumption.

concepts.label: canonical largest-prime supplier fibre
concepts.description: Bases N in [X,2X) whose pivot argument factors as cofactor times a large prime; the cofactor-one fibre is the shifted primes.

concepts.label: first-harmonic anchor defect
concepts.description: ∑_{N∈T}(2 − 2·windowFirstCos), the squared distance of the phase vector from the constant phase 1.

concepts.label: fibre variance and pairwise energy
concepts.description: Finite bias–variance and pairwise-energy identities that convert separated-pair counts into anchor defect.

concepts.label: infinite tail-orbit phase
concepts.description: The first character of the exact tail difference, equal to the character of the scaled series 2^N(2^h−1)S.

concepts.label: adjacent window step
concepts.description: The displacement between window discrepancies at consecutive bases N and N+1 at fixed depth.

concepts.label: adjacent carry tube
concepts.description: The strict branch of adjacent robust failure, affinely conjugate to the existing carryOrbit at shifted base N+L.

concepts.label: dyadic real
concepts.description: A real some power-of-two multiple of which is an integer; non-dyadicity is strictly weaker than irrationality at a fixed shift.

concepts.label: cofinal producer hypothesis (DTW predicate)
concepts.description: An unproved cofinal analytic/arithmetic supply statement declared as a Prop and consumed by the certificate machinery.

concepts.label: cofinal certificate supply reduces to #249
concepts.description: The pre-existing theorem that a cofinal supply of certified kills at every period h proves the totient series irrational.

concepts.label: Conditional peripheral-and-centred assembly for the #249 first-harmonic route
concepts.description: Both eventual peripheral estimates and the cofinal centered estimate at one shared depth function remain explicit hypotheses; no analytic supplier and no unconditional irrationality follow.

concepts.label: Exact finite arithmetic and run-threshold checks for #249
concepts.description: One finite parameter tuple plus an exact Farey denominator lemma and corrected finite run threshold; no cofinal certificate producer follows.

concepts.label: Generic centering countermodel for the #249 decomposition
concepts.description: A two-point complex countermodel to an inference; it is not a counterexample to the arithmetic totient-centered predicate.

concepts.label: One unconditional finite first-harmonic gap instance
concepts.description: Only (h,X,L)=(1,4,9) with bound 21X/25; no DTWFirstHarmonicNormGap or cofinal statement.

concepts.label: Finite peripheral estimates assemble into PivotBudgetAt
concepts.description: Assembles explicit cardinal and norm estimates into PivotBudgetAt; it proves neither the prime-distribution estimates nor the centered estimate.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the first harmonic of the window residue has a constant saving on a nonempty finite set T of bases inside a dyadic block [X,2X) — sum of cosines at most (9/10)|T| — and the depth satisfies the room inequality 16(2X+h+L+2) ≤ 2^L, then some N in T carries a kill certificate at depth L. The complex-norm form (norm of the phase sum at most 21X/25) and the anchor-defect form (defect at least |T|/5) are the same statement in different dress.
statement_nodes.engine: contrapositive averaging: if no base in T is certified, the room inequality puts every residue phase within π/8 of a full turn, forcing each cosine above 9/10
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary averaging plus a monotonicity bound on cos; no arithmetic input about the totient enters. The content is the interface, not the estimate.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Writing r for windowDiscrepancy(h,N,L) modulo 2^L, the real and complex first harmonics are exactly windowFirstCos(h,N,L) = cos(2πr/2^L) and windowFirstExp(h,N,L) = exp(i·2πr/2^L). The complex character has real part equal to the real first harmonic and unit norm, and it equals the character of the unreduced integer window discrepancy (reduction mod 2^L is invisible to the character).
Two bases whose window discrepancies agree modulo 2^L have exactly equal first-harmonic phases (and cosines); no choice of integer representative or analytic approximation remains at the call site.

Any proposed one-dimensional prime pivot phase can be removed from the window phase by exact division, so the window phase is the product of a residual weight and the pivot phase identically. This is a definition-plus-identity, not an independence claim: the residual retains the full coupling.

On the canonical largest-prime supplier bases the totient of the pivot argument factors as φ(cofactor)·(p−1), and the canonical cofactor-one fibre at overlap s = L−h is exactly the set of bases N in [X,2X) with N+h+1 prime.
statement_nodes.engine: canonical maximum-prime-factor selector with an explicit multiplication receipt
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Uses φ(mp) = φ(m)(p−1) for p not dividing m, a Mathlib-level classical fact; the content is that the sampled fibre is the genuine shifted-prime set, not a surrogate.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The iff mem_pivotFiber_one_overlap_iff holds only under the side conditions 4 ≤ X and h ≤ L, which the canonical statement above suppresses; outside them the cofactor-one fibre is not asserted to be the shifted-prime set. Both sides of the iff are decidable finite conditions, so this equivalence is not a restatement of any open problem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The block sum of window phases splits exactly into four evaluator-visible terms: centred correlation on good supplier bases, fibre-mean contribution, bad-cofactor contribution, and non-supplier contribution.

If the four pivot-decomposition terms obey the one-sided budget (centred real part at most 14X/25, and norms at most X/100, X/100 and 8X/25), then the block first-harmonic gap 9/10 holds. The budget arithmetic 14/25 + 1/100 + 1/100 + 8/25 = 9/10 is the whole content.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Triangle inequality plus rational arithmetic on the four budget constants.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two unproved cofinal first-harmonic hypotheses each imply irrationality of the #249 totient series: a cofinal complex-norm saving on dyadic blocks, and a cofinal four-term pivot budget. Neither hypothesis is proved anywhere in the corpus.
open_antecedents: DTWFirstHarmonicNormGap: for every h > 0 and every X₀ there exist X ≥ max X₀ 1 and L with room and ‖∑_{N ∈ Ico X (2X)} windowFirstExp h N L‖ ≤ (21/25)·X

DTWPivotResidualDecorrelation: for every h > 0 there exist an overlap s > 0 and η ∈ (0,1) such that cofinally PivotBudgetAt h X L s η holds, whose binding piece is (pivotCenteredCorrelation h X L s η).re ≤ (14/25)·X

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Sliding the base by one translates the window residue by exactly the fresh endpoint totient-difference letter, and that translation is exactly invertible: the adjacent step residue and the original window residue determine each other modulo 2^L.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The module prose reads this as 'adjacency exposes no independent arithmetic coordinate'. The Lean statement is an invertible translation identity, not a no-go theorem; it is recorded here as normalisation, not as a barrier.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the adjacent step residue lies in the robust central arc [2W, 2^L − 2W] with W = N+h+L+2, the endpoint certificate fires at the original base N; and under the room inequality the commonly proposed middle third of the dyadic circle is contained in that robust arc.
statement_nodes.engine: exact inverse translation by the endpoint letter, whose absolute value is below W
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Integer interval arithmetic on top of the translation identity; the interest is that the middle-third event certifies the base N itself rather than one member of a pair.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The finite window discrepancy divided by 2^L is the exact depth-L prefix of the tail difference R_{N+h} − R_N, the only omitted term being the translated tail difference at shifted base N+L, also divided by 2^L.

The adjacent window step divided by 2^L equals the current tail difference minus the known endpoint totient letter, plus an error that is a difference of two adjacent tail strips over 2^L and is bounded in absolute value by (2N + 2L + 2h + 5)/2^L.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Quantitative form of the claim that adjacency is a translate of existing data rather than a second arithmetic sample. It bounds the error; it does not prove that no method can exploit adjacency, and indeed the same lane derives a working two-point consumer and a carry transport from it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Any two distinct bases in a dyadic block whose first-harmonic phases have squared chord separation at least 19/25 force a certificate at one member of the pair, under the room inequality.
statement_nodes.engine: parallelogram law on two unit vectors, feeding the two-element case of the subset consumer
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Sharp two-point geometry: unit norms plus the parallelogram identity give Re(z+w) ≤ 9/5.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two unproved cofinal adjacent-separation hypotheses each imply #249 irrationality: cofinal adjacent middle-third occupancy, and cofinal squared chord separation 19/25 of an adjacent phase pair. Neither is proved.
open_antecedents: DTWAdjacentMiddleThirdSeparation: for every h > 0 and X₀ there exist X, L, N with room and AdjacentMiddleThirdAt h N L, i.e. 2^L ≤ 6·adjacentStepResidue ≤ 5·2^L
DTWAdjacentPhaseSeparation: for every h > 0 and X₀ there exist X, L, N with room and (19/25) ≤ ‖windowFirstExp h (N+1) L − windowFirstExp h N L‖²
statement_nodes.engine: composition through the finite consumers

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Failure of the robust adjacent arc selects a canonical short signed representative of the adjacent step residue with absolute value below 2W; under 4W < 2^L that representative is the unique such integer in its residue class.
statement_nodes.engine: two-sided partition of the failure region plus strict-bound uniqueness of a modular representative

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A robust adjacent-arc failure at depth with 4W < 2^L forces at least one of three things (the Lean conclusion is an inclusive disjunction, not an exclusive trichotomy, even though the case split on |adjacentWindowLift| against W is exclusive): the original same-base kill certificate fires; or the tail difference R_{N+h} − R_N is provably not an integer via the boundary-equality case; or the adjacent carry state lies inside the strict candidate box |c| ≤ N+L+h+1 of the existing survivor machinery.
statement_nodes.engine: trichotomy on |adjacentWindowLift| against the endpoint radius W
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The boundary branch is a genuine non-integrality certificate that the strict certifiedKill predicate does not capture; this is the kind of third case whose omission caused the earlier overclaim, and it is recorded explicitly here.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Across a run of consecutive robust adjacent failures with enough dyadic room, the adjacent carry state obeys c ↦ 2c − deltaTotient and is therefore exactly the existing carryOrbit at shifted base N+L started from the initial adjacent carry state.
statement_nodes.engine: modulus removal across two consecutive failures, then induction on the run length
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Transports the adjacent-window lane into CarrySurvivorExtinction rather than creating a second extinction theory.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An existing finite survivor-kill certificate at shifted base N+L, together with dyadic room along the run, forces within K steps either a same-base kill certificate or a boundary non-integrality certificate at some base N+i.
statement_nodes.engine: contradiction against the carry-orbit escape supplied by survivorKill

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The tail difference R_{N+h} − R_N equals the scaled series 2^N(2^h−1)·S minus an explicit integer prefix difference, so the first character of the tail difference is exactly the first character of the scaled series orbit; that orbit is a unit-modulus squaring orbit.
The finite-window phase and the infinite tail-orbit phase differ by an explicit rotation, with ‖windowFirstExp − tailOrbitFirstExp‖ < 2π(N+L+h+2)/2^L.
statement_nodes.engine: exact factorisation plus the elementary bound ‖e^{ix} − 1‖ ≤ |x| and the universal totient-tail strip

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Any real-part gap in the infinite tail orbit survives truncation to depth L with exactly the supplied additive error: if (tailOrbitFirstExp h N).re ≤ a and the truncation budget is at most ε, then windowFirstCos h N L ≤ a + ε; the 4/5 orbit gap with budget 1/10 gives the 9/10 finite gap the consumer wants.
statement_nodes.engine: triangle inequality against the truncation bound

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any base and any positive error budget there is a depth, beyond any prescribed threshold, that simultaneously satisfies the certificate room inequality and drives the phase-truncation error below the budget.
statement_nodes.engine: geometric decay of (c + L)·2^{-L}
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard geometric-linear limit; it is what removes all depth bookkeeping from the remaining arithmetic hypotheses.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A unit-modulus squaring orbit that never reaches 1 has cofinally many adjacent chords of length at least 1. No equidistribution or measure input is used.
statement_nodes.engine: the deficit y = 1 − Re z triples at each step while staying below 1/2, which is impossible
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary expansivity of the doubling map near the fixed point 1; folklore, stated here for complex orbits rather than for angles.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At a single fixed shift h, if (2^h − 1)·S is not a dyadic rational then the scaled orbit has cofinally many adjacent chords of length at least 1, and hence the fixed-shift fibre-free counted-separated-pairs socket DTWWindowSeparatedPairsAt h holds. Non-dyadicity at one shift is strictly weaker than irrationality of S.
open_antecedents: ¬ IsDyadicReal (((2:ℝ)^h − 1) * ∑' n, (φ n)/2^n) at the fixed shift h — no value of h is known for which this is proved
statement_nodes.engine: expansivity of the squaring orbit
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the weaker sibling engine of the shift-uniform statement. Irrationality does imply DTWWindowSeparatedPairsAt h at every h (the barrier proof establishes it shift by shift), so the barrier direction covers this predicate; what is missing is the converse for a single shift, because the forward consumer needs the predicate at every h. Hence no equivalence is established at any single h and the predicate stays a live target. That it is genuinely weaker is not proved — only that it follows from the weaker hypothesis ¬IsDyadicReal ((2^h−1)·S), which irrationality also implies.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Lean statement is the implication: irrationality of the #249 series implies the fibre-free counted-separated-pairs socket at every positive shift. It is classed as a barrier rather than as a producer because its antecedent is the target itself: together with the forward consumer in the same file it shows the socket cannot be a strictly weaker intermediate obligation, so proving it is not a partial result short of #249.
open_antecedents: Irrational (∑' n, (φ n)/2ⁿ) — the antecedent of this implication is Erdős #249 itself; the theorem is recorded as a barrier on the socket, never as evidence for it
statement_nodes.engine: expansivity of the scaled squaring orbit plus the explicit two-point sample {N, N+1} at a depth where both finite phases are within 1/20 of the orbit
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Flagged as a restatement because its single hypothesis IS Erdős #249: as a standalone Lean statement it proves nothing unconditional about the totient series. Its barrier reading is valid only jointly with the forward consumer irrational_totient_series_of_windowSeparatedPairs in the same file; neither leg alone is progress.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: It closes only DTWWindowSeparatedPairs, the shift-uniform fibre-free counted-separated-pairs predicate, and 'closes' means only that the predicate is not a weaker obligation than #249 — not that it is false or useless. Precision point: irrationality DOES supply the fixed-shift predicate DTWWindowSeparatedPairsAt h at every h > 0 (that is literally how this theorem is proved, one shift at a time), so the barrier direction reaches the fixed-shift predicate. What is NOT established for a single shift is the converse: the forward consumer irrational_totient_series_of_windowSeparatedPairs quantifies over every h, so no single DTWWindowSeparatedPairsAt h is shown to imply #249, and it therefore remains a live target — one moreover implied by the weaker hypothesis of non-dyadicity of (2^h−1)·S. No separation is proved, so 'strictly weaker' is not a corpus result. Beyond that the theorem does NOT close: (ii) any pivot-fibre socket (anti-reconstruction, reconstruction variance, pairwise energy, separated pairs, window pairwise energy, window separated pairs), none of which is shown to follow from irrationality; (iii) the natural-prime sockets (window gap, point escape, prime tail-orbit gap, strict prime tail-orbit gap); (iv) the adjacent-separation sockets; (v) the first-harmonic norm-gap and pivot-budget sockets. It also does not say the socket is false or useless — it remains a correct sufficient condition, only not a weaker one.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The fibre-free counted-separated-pairs socket is logically equivalent to irrationality of the #249 totient series. Both sides are open; the equivalence is a geometric reformulation of the open problem, not progress on it.
open_antecedents: Irrational (∑' n, (φ n)/2^n) — Erdős #249 itself, open

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A cofinal supply of counted separated pairs of window phases on any nonempty subset of a cofinal dyadic block implies #249 irrationality. Since the converse also holds, the hypothesis is a restatement of the open problem.
open_antecedents: DTWWindowSeparatedPairs: for every h > 0 and X₀ there exist X, L, a nonempty T ⊆ Ico X (2X), a pair set P ⊆ T×T and δ ≥ 0 with common separation δ and mass 2·|T|²/5 ≤ |P|·δ² — proved equivalent to Erdős #249 itself
statement_nodes.engine: pairwise energy to anchor defect to the subset consumer

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Standard finite complex identities: sum of squared norms equals centred energy plus card times squared mean; total pairwise energy equals 2·card times centred energy; a counted set of separated ordered pairs lower-bounds pairwise energy by |P|δ²; and pairwise energy at 2|T|²/5 forces squared distance |T|/5 from any fixed anchor.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bias–variance decomposition and the pairwise-energy identity for finite vector families; textbook material, formalised here for complex finite sums.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The anchor defect of a finite base set equals 2|T| − 2·(sum of first-harmonic cosines), equals the sum of squared distances of the phases from the constant phase 1, and the threshold |T|/5 on the defect is exactly, in both directions, the 9/10 first-harmonic threshold on the same set.

The pivot reconstruction error equals the window anchor error (windowFirstExp − 1) rotated by the conjugate pivot phase, and its fibre sum is exactly the residual-weighted mode minus the bare conjugate-pivot mode. No independence or phase-only surrogate is introduced.

Centred reconstruction-error energy on a supplier fibre is exactly normalised pairwise energy, so a pairwise-energy bound at 2|F|²/5 gives fibre variance at least |F|/5 with the unknown fibre mean eliminated.

The fibre reconstruction defect equals 2|F| − 2·Re(window mode), equals the sum of squared distances of the residuals from the locked reconstruction conj(phase), and equals centred variance plus card times squared bias.

Exact two-mode formula for centred fibre variance, V = 2|F| − 2Re W₀ − ‖W₁ − C₁‖²/|F|; and if Re W₀ ≤ (4/5)|F| together with normalised anti-lock ‖(W₁ − C₁)/|F|‖ ≤ 2/5 (implied by ‖W₁‖ ≤ |F|/3 and ‖C₁‖ ≤ |F|/15), then V ≥ (6/25)|F|, strictly above the consumer's |F|/5.
statement_nodes.engine: bias–variance identity combined with the triangle inequality on the two modes
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Constant bookkeeping on top of the exact identity; the mode bounds themselves are hypotheses, not results.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A single supplier fibre supplies a certificate under any of a descending chain of finite intake conditions: anchor defect at least |F|/5; centred variance at least |F|/5; reconstruction-error pairwise energy at least 2|F|²/5; a counted separated-pair set of that mass; the same two conditions for the raw window phases with no pivot weighting.
statement_nodes.engine: variance and pairwise-energy identities feeding the subset first-harmonic consumer
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Each is a composition of the identities above with the finite consumer; the mathematics is the interface layering, not a new estimate.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The unproved cofinal producer hypotheses of this lane are ordered by proved implications: counted separated pairs imply pairwise energy imply variance imply anti-reconstruction; raw window separated pairs imply window pairwise energy imply anti-reconstruction and also imply the fibre-free socket; two-mode cancellation implies the natural window gap and the variance socket; and the prime tail-orbit gap implies the natural point escape.
statement_nodes.engine: forgetting structure (factorisation data, centring, weighting) while retaining the sample and the counted mass
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: These edges relate hypotheses to hypotheses. Every node in the order is unproved, so the order records where a future estimate would have to land, not any progress on #249.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Eight unproved cofinal pivot-fibre hypotheses each imply irrationality of the #249 totient series, all by composition through the fibre intake and the certificate-supply reduction. None of the hypotheses is proved anywhere in the corpus.

statement_nodes.scope_caveat: None of the eight sockets is known to be weaker than #249: each implies it, so proving any one of them is at least as hard as proving #249. One of them is provably no easier than a statement already known to be exactly as hard: windowSeparatedPairs_of_pivotWindowSeparatedPairs (line 1377) sends DTWPivotWindowSeparatedPairs into DTWWindowSeparatedPairs, which dtwWindowSeparatedPairs_iff_irrational_totient_series proves equivalent to #249. These endpoints therefore record where an estimate would have to land, not any reduction in difficulty.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two unproved pointwise hypotheses imply #249 irrationality: a cofinal single-base escape below 9/10 inside the canonical shifted-prime fibre, and a cofinal prime-indexed real-part gap at 4/5 in the exact infinite tail orbit. Neither is proved.

statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Reclassified from not_assessed on adversarial review. naturalPivotPointEscape_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap is line-for-line the legacy proof naturalPivotPointEscape_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitGap (PivotAntiReconstruction.lean:1246) with the fixed budget ε = 1/10 replaced by ε = 9/10 − Re; every other step (fibre membership via mem_pivotFiber_one_overlap_iff, depth via exists_natural_window_depth_with_error, transport via windowFirstCos_le_add_of_tailOrbitGap) is reused unchanged. It is a routine weakening of an existing node, not a new engine. The hypothesis is weaker than DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitGap (Re ≤ 4/5 implies Re < 9/10), but no Lean declaration in the corpus formalises that implication, and no separation is proved, so 'strictly weaker' is an informal remark rather than a corpus result.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The producer DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap is unproved: no prime p is known for which (tailOrbitFirstExp h (p−h−1)).re < 9/10 is established, at any h. Calling it the weakest live producer is a statement about hypothesis strength within this lane only; it is not evidence that it is attainable.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The exact phase recurrence iterates: for every shift h and offsets M,k, tailOrbitFirstExp h (M+k) = (tailOrbitFirstExp h M)^(2^k). The initial phase is the scaled angle of (2^h−1) times the totient series, and phase 1 is equivalent to an integral tail difference. Consequently the cofinal strict-prime gap producer is equivalent to a power-of-two orbit condition on the single initial phase at each shift; non-dyadic initial phase yields only a conditional cofinal nonpositive-phase route.
statement_nodes.engine: Induction on the offset using the exact squaring recurrence; the integer carry is absorbed as a full 2π rotation.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A normal-form classification of the existing strict-gap producer, not an additional prime-distribution result or an endpoint theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The initial-phase equivalence supplies no real-part gap and does not prove that the actual totient phase enters a useful region.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a tail-orbit phase reaches 1, or more generally a dyadic root that reaches 1 under finitely many squarings, the cofinal natural-prime strict-gap producer is impossible for that shift.
statement_nodes.engine: An absorbing phase remains 1 under the squaring dynamics, contradicting the strict real-part bound required by the producer.
